answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work; the protocol randomly assigns tasks and slashes that stake when independent checks confirm fabricated results. Creating a hundred identities therefore requires funding a hundred locks, while one real identity can reuse its stake over time. The dune, summit, and haven markets can each set different stake sizes, but none should treat identity count alone as proof of trust. The attacker pays capital and risks losing it for every fake agent, making cheap Sybil flooding costly rather than merely inconvenient.
